# php2shell checker

> Free, open-source, read-only checker for php2shell: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in PHP itself. Fixed in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. PHP 8.1 and older get no upstream fix.

Author: Ariful Islam (https://arifulislamat.com). License: MIT. Last updated: 2026-10-22.

## Key facts

- php2shell is CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in the PHP runtime.
- Any site running a vulnerable PHP version is affected: WordPress, Laravel, Drupal, Joomla and custom PHP.
- Fixed versions: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35. PHP 8.1 and older: no upstream fix; upgrade to 8.2+ or use a vendor backport (Ubuntu Pro, Debian LTS, CloudLinux).
- Updating WordPress, Laravel or plugins does not fix it. Only updating PHP does, followed by restarting PHP-FPM, Apache or LiteSpeed.
- Apache mod_php is the highest-risk setup: the attack starts before any application code runs.
- Ubuntu, Debian and RHEL may backport the fix without changing the PHP version number.
- Interim mitigation (not a fix): in php.ini or the PHP-FPM pool set session.upload_progress.enabled = 0, plus fatal_error_backtraces = 0 on PHP 8.5; for CVE-2026-109618 a non-overridable memory_limit = -1 with container memory limits and post_max_size = 8M. A WAF such as Cloudflare reduces exposure but is not a fix.
- Advisories: https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w and https://github.com/php/php-src/security/advisories/GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp

## How to check

1. On the server (most accurate: PHP builds, distro backports, containers, signs of compromise):
   `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arifulislamat/php2shell-audit/main/check.sh | sudo bash`
2. From any computer, against a website:
   `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/arifulislamat/php2shell-audit/main/check.sh | bash -s -- https://example.com`
3. In the browser: https://arifulislamat.github.io/php2shell-audit/

The checker sends no exploit payloads and changes nothing. Exit codes: 0 nothing found, 1 vulnerable PHP, 2 possible compromise, 3 site unreachable, 4 PHP found but version unconfirmed.
